Dear Jeffrey,
how are you?
We came back from Germany on Tuesday evening. I visited a couple conferences and a symposium, and got a
best paper award for a piece on equipping Al with motivation. At the moment, I am working with a psychologist
on translating the motivation theory into what we hope will become a model of personality, which we can then
test. Another thing that I a currently experiment with is a type of semantic/neural network that instead of
activations passes several simple types of messages to facilitate learning and self-organization. The basic idea is
to find out if we can replace the global operations that are for instance done in backpropagation (where an
algorithm looks like God's eye at a complete layer of neurons in a neural net) by local operations (where each
neuron only talks to its directly connected neighbors, and no central control exists). In a sense, each node
becomes something like an information broker that gets rewards for computing predictions for his neighbors,
based on information he buys or commissions from his neighbors. I am curious if this is a better or an equivalent
paradigm to energy (as for instance in Boltzmann machines). While I was in Berlin, I sat down with my MicroPsi
group (Priska also visited this summer in Cambridge). We are working on getting our agent simulation to do stuff
in a computer game world.
Other than that, I am hanging out every week at Marvin Minsky's, and help getting their Minskitute started. I
hope that there is a chance to build a critical mass to initiate work on his classical ideas (especially Society of
Mind), despite the fascinating political difficulties.
Last but not least, I will teach a seminar on the Future of Artificial Intelligence at the Media Lab.
Bests, and grateful greetings,
Joscha
